fields.description: A big, courteous man with a heart condition he refuses to discuss. He collects clocks, maps and quarrels in about equal measure, and has the gift of making every guest feel they are his favourite.
Composed, quick and fond of crossword puzzles and cold tea. She runs the household in all but name and has long since learned which of her husband's disputes to ignore.
Charming, restless and always somewhere else in his head. He served with distinction, drinks a little too much, and owes money in more than one town.
Quiet, exact and easy to overlook, which she uses. She types faster than she speaks and knows where every paper in the house is kept.
Urbane, silver-haired and fond of telling stories at his own expense. He has handled the Thornes' affairs for twenty years and is everyone's idea of a safe pair of hands.
A brisk, kind man with large hands and a habit of patting his pockets. He has treated Sir Alaric's heart for eight years and is more worried about it than he lets on.
Tall, grave and perfectly silent on the stairs. He has served the Thornes for thirty years and measures his own worth by how little anyone ever notices him.

Square, rosy and entirely unflappable. She feeds the household, manages the maids and notices everything that passes through her kitchen. She dislikes gossip and will tell you anything if you are kind to her.
Quick, nervous and kind. She has worked at the Hall for two years, sees the whole house before anyone else is up, and is terrified of Mr. Pell.
A solid, patient man on a bicycle, with a notebook and a strong sense of what is and is not his business. He has never had a case bigger than a stolen pig.

fields.description: A low, wet estate of reed beds, drove roads and willows, set on a rise of firmer ground in the fens. The nearest village is Saltreach, two and a half miles away by the causeway.
A raised gravel road across the marsh, covered by the mere at the highest tides. In a hard south-westerly it can be impassable for hours.
A small fenland village of brick cottages, a church, a public house and a police constable. The only telephone exchange for miles is in the post office.
A brick lodge at the end of the drive, empty since the old gardener retired. The estate's telephone line comes in here before running to the hall on a line of poles.
A rambling red-brick house with a Jacobean core, Victorian additions and a conservatory that never quite matched either. Wind finds its way into every passage.
A flagged hall with a grandfather clock, a long oak settle and a staircase that creaks on the fourth step. The butler's pantry opens off it.
Walls of leather spines, a worn Turkey carpet, a tray of decanters and a deep fireplace. The mantel is carved with a date in Roman numerals. A door in the east wall leads to the study.
A small, orderly room with a roll-top desk, a portrait of Sir Alaric's father and a framed estate map. A typewriter sits under a cover on a side table.
Chintz sofas, a baby grand nobody plays and a tall window onto the drive. After dinner the household gathers here for coffee.
A long mahogany table under a dim chandelier, with twelve chairs and a sideboard that is polished every morning whether or not anyone eats.
A flagged kitchen with a vast range, copper pans and a scrubbed table where the staff take their meals. A door leads to the yard and another to the cellar steps.
A glass-and-iron room of potted palms and wicker chairs. A garden door opens onto a gravel path to the boathouse.
A long first-floor corridor with doors to the family and guest bedrooms. Floorboards creak, and a light under a door can be seen from the stairs.
A cool vaulted cellar of wine racks, coal and trunks. The house's main fuse board is bolted to the wall by the steps.
A tarred wooden shed on the edge of the mere with a slipway, a stack of nets and a flat-bottomed punt. A damp path through the reeds leads up to the conservatory.

truth.label: What happened in the library
truth.truth: Julian Ashcombe, the family's solicitor and a trustee of the Thorne Trust, had taken about eleven thousand four hundred pounds over six years by paying it to a fictitious 'M. Rutherford'. Verity Lorne noticed the pattern while indexing the papers and told Sir Alaric on Thursday. Sir Alaric invited Ashcombe to confront him on Saturday after breakfast and asked the valuer to attend as an independent witness. At about five to eleven on Friday night Ashcombe fetched a clean glass from the kitchen; at five past he joined Sir Alaric in the library for a brandy to 'talk through the papers', and put a lethal dose of digitalis tincture, taken from Dr. Farrant's bag in the drawing room, into his host's glass. Sir Alaric's known heart condition and prescription meant that his death would pass as natural. Ashcombe rinsed his own glass, burned a page of the ledger, left by the conservatory door and went back to bed.

economy.regions.label: Regions (US states, DC and the national baseline)

basis.summary: Rounded, approximate state-level figures compiled from well-known public statistics as recalled; not queried live. Intended as plausible defaults, not as authoritative statistics.
basis.state_income_tax_effective_pct: Approximate effective state income tax as a percent of gross wages for a single filer earning about $60,000 (a middle-income band), after the state standard deduction/exemptions; derived from published 2025 state brackets (Tax Foundation / state revenue departments). Rounded to 0.1. Excludes local income taxes (see local_income_tax_pct_typical) and payroll-type state levies such as CA SDI.
basis.sales_tax_combined_avg_pct: Tax Foundation 2025 combined state plus population-weighted average local sales tax rate; rounded to 0.01. Hawaii and Alaska values are approximations of the GET / local-only rate.
basis.cost_of_living_multiplier: US = 1.00. Approximate from BEA Regional Price Parities (all items, 2022-2023 vintage) smoothed to 2025; rounded to 0.01.
basis.median_rent_cents_per_month: Approximate asking-rent medians for 1BR and 2BR units, a blend of Zumper, Apartment List and HUD FY2025 Fair Market Rent state patterns, rounded to $10. 1BR is the anchor; 2BR is derived as 1BR times a regional ratio (Northeast 1.22, Midwest 1.27, South 1.27, West 1.24; DC uses South) rounded to $10. Statewide medians hide large metro-vs-rural spread.
basis.residential_electricity_cents_per_kwh: EIA Electric Power Monthly, average residential retail price by state, 2024 annual / 2025 year-to-date, rounded to 0.5 cent. Decimal value in cents (not dollars) per kWh. US average is about 17 cents.
basis.minimum_wage_cents_per_hour: Effective statutory floor in 2025 for non-tipped adult workers: the higher of the state rate and the federal $7.25. Where rates vary by locality or employer size (NY, OR, MN) the statewide/largest-area figure is used.

scope.doc: `national` is the single baseline row `us` (multiplier 1.00); the state-only columns are absent on it.

state_income_tax_effective_pct.doc: Single filer at about $60,000, after the state standard deduction; excludes local and payroll levies.

cost_of_living_multiplier.doc: US = 1.00. Applied by the economy pack at pricing time, never baked into rows.

minimum_wage_cents_per_h.doc: Effective 2025 floor, the higher of state and federal.

nd.name: North Dakota

oh.name: Ohio

pa.name: Pennsylvania

sd.name: South Dakota

tn.name: Tennessee

tx.name: Texas

wa.name: Washington

source.reflectsPeriod: 2025-2026 (rates as of late 2025; Fed funds target 3.50-3.75% after the Dec 2025 cut)
source.basis: Rounded typical consumer-finance parameters recalled from Federal Reserve G.19 and H.15, FDIC national rates, Freddie Mac PMMS, Bankrate / Edmunds surveys, CFPB, KFF Employer Health Benefits Survey 2025, Vanguard How America Saves 2025, IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40 and IRS notices for 2025/2026; not queried live. Treat as plausible defaults.

values.doc: The section as in the source. Keys containing `cents` are integer cents, keys containing `pct` are percent units; ranges are {min, typical, max}.

fed_funds_target_pct.note: Target range after the December 2025 FOMC cut; was 4.25-4.50 for most of H1 2025.

apr_pct.note: Fed G.19 average on accounts assessed interest is ~22%; new-offer averages ~24%; best-credit cards 15-18%, subprime 28-30%.

grace_period_days.note: No interest if the previous balance is paid in full; none on cash advances.

minimum_payment.formula: min(statement_balance + interest + fees, max(floor_cents, ceil(statement_balance * principal_pct / 100 + interest_this_cycle + fees_this_cycle)))

variants.issuer_style: 1% of balance plus interest and fees
2% of balance, no extra interest add-on

minimum_payment.interest_per_cycle: balance * apr_pct / 100 / 12 (monthly periodic rate; issuers use average daily balance with daily rate = apr/365)

late_fee_cents.note: Reg Z safe-harbor amounts for 2025 ($32 first, $43 repeat); the CFPB $8 cap was vacated in April 2025. Issuers commonly charge $30-$41.

cash_advance_fee.note: No grace period; interest starts the same day.

high_yield.note: Online banks; floating with the Fed funds rate.

checking_apy_pct.note: Most checking accounts pay near zero; a few reward accounts pay 3-4% up to a balance cap.

monthly_maintenance.note: Often waived with direct deposit or a minimum balance ($1,000-$1,500).

atm_out_of_network_total.note: Bankrate-style average ~$4.73 (operator surcharge plus bank fee).

overdraft.note: Average ~$27; many banks have cut or eliminated overdraft fees; cap per day typical 3 charges.

auto.payment_formula: payment = P * r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n), r = apr_pct/100/12, n = term_months

apr_pct_30yr_fixed.note: Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year averaged about 6.3-6.9% through 2025; borrowers with lower credit pay more.

pmi_pct_per_year.note: Applies when down payment is under 20%.

property_tax_pct_of_value_per_year.note: Effective rate; varies by state and county.

homeowners_insurance_cents_per_month.note: Higher in hurricane, hail and wildfire areas.

apr_pct.note: Fed G.19 24-month personal loan average ~12%; online lenders 7-36%.

payday.note: High-cost; usually avoided; included for debt-trap scenarios.

investing.title: Investing (index return model, GBM recipe, bonds, cash)

broad_us_equity_index.description: Total-return broad US stock index (S&P 500 style) for seeded price paths; use geometric Brownian motion with these parameters.
broad_us_equity_index.long_run_basis: 1926-2024 nominal total return ~10% geometric, ~12% arithmetic, ~19% volatility; modern-era (post-1990) volatility ~15-17%; the typical 5-year-ahead expectation is lower, ~6-8% nominal.
broad_us_equity_index.gbm_note: S(t+dt) = S(t) * exp((mu - sigma^2/2) dt + sigma sqrt(dt) Z) with mu=0.11, sigma=0.16 per year; use a seeded RNG.

retirement_account_limits_cents.note: IRS limits for 2025; 2026 values as announced in IRS Notice 2025-67 (401(k) $24,500, catch-up $8,000, IRA $7,500).

single.note: KFF 2025: average worker contribution ~$1,440/yr (about 16% of a ~$9,300 premium) for single coverage.

family.note: KFF 2025: average worker contribution ~$6,850/yr (~26% of a ~$27,000 premium).

health_deductible_cents.note: Annual deductible; KFF average single deductible ~ $1,800 in 2025.

employer_match_typical.formula: 50% of the first 6% of pay (3% of pay)

retirement_401k.note: Vanguard How America Saves 2025: average deferral ~7.7% (12% total with employer); most common auto-enroll default 3-4%.

garnishment.note: Federal CCPA limits; not applied by default.

values.effective_withholding_note: occupations.json withholding_rate_pct was computed from these parameters.

pickup_midsize.name: Midsize pickup (Tacoma / Colorado class)
pickup_midsize.notes: Cargo is the open bed (about 5 ft). Towing about 6,500 lb.

pickup_fullsize.name: Full-size pickup (F-150 / Silverado class)
pickup_fullsize.notes: Cargo is the open bed (5.5-6.5 ft). Towing up to ~10,000 lb with the right package.

pickup_heavy_duty_diesel.name: Heavy-duty diesel pickup (2500 / F-250 class)
pickup_heavy_duty_diesel.notes: DEF fluid (diesel exhaust fluid) refills every ~5,000 miles, about $15-25/ 2.5 gal. Towing up to 15,000-20,000 lb.

suv_compact.name: Compact SUV (RAV4 / CR-V class)
suv_compact.notes: Cargo volume is with the rear seats folded: about 1,100 L; behind seats about 540 L. Hybrids reach 38-41 mpg.

suv_midsize_3row.name: Midsize three-row SUV (Highlander / Explorer class)
suv_midsize_3row.notes: Cargo with second and third rows folded about 2,300 L; behind the third row about 480 L.

minivan.name: Minivan (Sienna / Odyssey / Pacifica class)
minivan.notes: Hybrid minivans (Sienna) return 35-36 mpg combined; cargo with rows folded is about 4,000 L (140 cu ft).

ev_sedan.name: Electric sedan (Model 3 / Ioniq 6 class)
ev_sedan.notes: No oil changes. Many states add an EV registration surcharge of about $100-$250 per year, included in the registration band. Tires wear faster (instant torque, weight).

ev_crossover.name: Electric crossover (Model Y / Equinox EV class)
ev_crossover.notes: Cargo volume with rear seats folded.

motorcycle_standard.name: Motorcycle, standard or cruiser (500-900 cc)
motorcycle_standard.notes: Cargo is saddlebags or a tail bag; a passenger seat is optional. Front/rear tires are replaced separately (rear wears ~2x faster). Helmet laws vary by state.

scooter_150.name: Scooter or moped (50-150 cc)
scooter_150.notes: Under-seat storage about 25-35 L. Mopeds under 50 cc often need no registration or license in some states; top speed 30-60 mph.

bass_boat_outboard.name: Outboard bass boat (18-20 ft, 150-200 hp)

maintenance.engine_service_note: oil, filters and lower-unit gear oil every 100 hours or annually

bass_boat_outboard.notes: Boat state registration usually renews every 1-3 years (annualised here); trailer is registered separately (~$30-$100/year). Price includes motor and trailer. Cruise burn is at planing speed with a normal load.

pontoon_boat.name: Pontoon boat (22-24 ft, 90-150 hp outboard)
pontoon_boat.notes: Capacity plate typically 8-13 persons / 1,500-2,500 lb total.

jet_ski_pwc.name: Personal watercraft / jet ski (1-3 seats)

maintenance.engine_service_note: oil and filter every 50 hours or annually

jet_ski_pwc.notes: Premium-grade fuel recommended by most makers. Price excludes trailer ($800-$2,500).

sailboat_auxiliary.name: Cruising sailboat with auxiliary diesel (30-35 ft)

consumption.note: Displacement hull: motors at hull speed (~6 knots) burning 0.6-1.0 gph; sailing uses no fuel.

maintenance.engine_service_note: oil and filters every 100-150 hours; impeller every 200 hours

sailboat_auxiliary.notes: Documented vessels (US Coast Guard documentation) pay no state registration. A rule of thumb is that ownership costs 10% of value per year. Sleeps 4-6.

atv_utility.name: ATV, utility quad (450-700 cc)
atv_utility.notes: Cargo: front and rear racks, about 40 kg front and 80 kg rear. Many states require an off-highway vehicle (OHV) sticker/permit rather than road registration; helmet and age rules vary.

utv_side_by_side.name: UTV / side-by-side (Ranger / RZR class, 2-4 seats)
utv_side_by_side.notes: Utility models carry a dump bed up to ~450 kg; sport models carry people only. Roll cage and belts required.

dirt_bike_250.name: Dirt bike, 250 cc four-stroke
dirt_bike_250.notes: Competition bikes are not street legal; plated dual-sport bikes use the motorcycle class. Premium fuel with 91+ octane typical.

four_door_saloon.name: Four-door saloon
four_door_saloon.notes: A dark green saloon, parked on the gravel forecourt with its bonnet to the house.

flat_bottomed_punt.name: Flat-bottomed punt
flat_bottomed_punt.notes: A long flat-bottomed punt with a pole and a pair of oars, tarred black.

source.reflectsPeriod: 2025-2026 (model-year 2025 new prices; used = about 3-5 years old)

basis.prices_and_economy: Typical new MSRP bands, used-market (Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book, NADA) values and EPA fueleconomy.gov combined ratings for representative models, rounded; marine and off-road from manufacturer spec sheets (Mercury, Yamaha, Sea-Doo, Polaris, Honda) and dealer pricing.
basis.insurance: Bankrate / Insurify 2025 average premiums: full coverage about $2,300-$2,700 per year for a clean-record adult, state-minimum liability about $600-$800 per year; EVs are 15-25% higher; boats about 1.5% of value per year; rounded to cents per month.
basis.maintenance: Manufacturer service schedules and AAA / RepairPal cost surveys, rounded.
basis.registration: State DMV fee ranges; actual cost varies by weight, value, age and county.

factors.doc: Factor id to consumption multiplier (>1 burns more). Road: relative to the combined rating; marine: to cruise_planing; off-road: to normal_trail.

road.basis: Multipliers on fuel (or energy) consumed per mile relative to the combined rating; >1 burns more. Rounded rules of thumb from EPA/fueleconomy.gov and AAA tests.
road.note: For EVs the same multipliers apply to kWh per mile (cold weather is harsher: use 1.35; highway 75 mph: 1.30; towing: 2.0).

marine.basis: Multipliers on gallons per hour at planing cruise; rules of thumb from engine makers' fuel curves (Mercury, Yamaha, Volvo Penta) and BoatUS guidance.
marine.note: Plan on the 1/3 out, 1/3 back, 1/3 reserve fuel rule. Marine tank capacities are usable gallons.

offroad.basis: Multipliers on gallons per hour at normal trail pace; rule-of-thumb values from OEM spec sheets and trail-riding reports.

lore_hall.title: Harrowmere Hall
lore_hall.content: Harrowmere Hall stands on a rise of firm ground in the fens, built round a Jacobean core and added to by every generation of Thornes. The west wing burned in 1887 and was rebuilt in a brisker brick. The house is damp, draughty and beloved; it is also famous for its collection of clocks and maps.

lore_thornes.title: The Thorne family
lore_thornes.content: The Thornes have held Harrowmere for three hundred years, and the baronetcy for two. They farmed the fen, drained it, lost money and made it back. The present family is Sir Alaric, Lady Honoria and, as heir, Sir Alaric's nephew Captain Rupert Thorne; the Thornes have no children of their own.

lore_causeway.title: The Mere Causeway
lore_causeway.content: The causeway is a raised gravel road of about two miles that connects the estate to Saltreach. At the highest tides, or when a gale pushes the mere up, it can be impassable for a day. Estate people know the tide tables by heart; visitors are told to check before they set out.

lore_saltreach.title: Saltreach
lore_saltreach.content: Saltreach is a village of about two hundred, with a church, a public house called the Heron, a post office with the district's telephone exchange and one police constable. The Thornes have been its principal family for as long as anyone remembers.

lore_collection.title: The Thorne collection
lore_collection.content: Sir Alaric's collection of English clocks and fen maps is one of the finest private ones in eastern England. This autumn he has decided to sell a selection at auction to fund repairs to the Hall, and he has invited a London valuer to appraise the pieces before the sale.

lore_alaric.title: Sir Alaric Thorne
lore_alaric.content: Sir Alaric Thorne is sixty-two, big, courteous and given to long stories about clocks. He has had a weak heart for eight years and takes drops from Dr. Farrant as directed, though he has been known to forget. He likes to host house parties and to settle disputes before breakfast.

lore_honoria.title: Lady Honoria Thorne
lore_honoria.content: Lady Honoria is Sir Alaric's wife of thirty-three years. She runs the house calmly and dryly, solves the newspaper's crossword every day and has never been known to raise her voice.

lore_rupert.title: Captain Rupert Thorne
lore_rupert.content: Captain Rupert Thorne is Sir Alaric's nephew and heir. Charming, restless and a little vague about money, he is said in Saltreach to owe more than he earns. His uncle has bailed him out twice and has said that he will not do so a third time.

lore_verity.title: Verity Lorne
lore_verity.content: Miss Verity Lorne has been Sir Alaric's secretary for four years. She is quiet, exact and loyal, and has never been late with a letter. The household calls her 'the filing cabinet' and relies on her to find anything.

lore_ashcombe.title: Julian Ashcombe
lore_ashcombe.content: Julian Ashcombe is the Thorne family's solicitor and a trustee of the family trust. He has handled their affairs for twenty years and is respected across the county. A frequent weekend guest, he is as much a part of the furniture as the grandfather clock.

lore_farrant.title: Dr. Lionel Farrant
lore_farrant.content: Dr. Farrant has been the family's physician for fifteen years, Sir Alaric's heart specialist for eight, and a friend for longer. He carries his black bag everywhere and puts it down wherever he stops.

lore_pell.title: Gideon Pell
lore_pell.content: Pell has been the Hall's butler for thirty years. He is tall, grave and impeccably discreet, and he holds the keys to the cellar, the plate cupboard and most of the household's secrets. He is also the one person who can say how the house is meant to run.

lore_marsh.title: Mrs. Dorothea Marsh
lore_marsh.content: Mrs. Marsh has cooked at the Hall for twenty years. She is solid, kind and unshockable, and her kitchen is the warmest room in the house. She dislikes gossip but will tell a friend a great deal.

lore_nell.title: Nell Sparrow
lore_nell.content: Nell Sparrow is nineteen, the Hall's youngest servant, and the first person up each morning. She lights the fires, dusts the library and is afraid of Mr. Pell. She sees the house before anyone else has made a mess of it.

lore_hobbs.title: Constable Albert Hobbs
lore_hobbs.content: Constable Hobbs has kept the peace in Saltreach for eleven years, mostly by bicycle. He is patient, thorough and slow to hurry, and has never had a case bigger than a stolen pig. He gets to the Hall as fast as the tide lets him.

lore_library.title: The Library
lore_library.content: The library is the heart of the house. It has leather-bound sets of the county histories, a worn Turkey carpet and a fireplace carved with the year the west wing was rebuilt. Guests are encouraged to take a book; Sir Alaric prefers that they put it back.

lore_study.title: Sir Alaric's study
lore_study.content: The study is Sir Alaric's private office. It holds a roll-top desk, the estate map and a wall safe behind the portrait of his father. It is generally known that he keeps important papers in the safe.

lore_conservatory.title: The Conservatory
lore_conservatory.content: The conservatory was added in 1902 and has never been warm. A garden door leads to a path through the reeds to the boathouse; the family use it in summer and the staff use it for shortcuts.

lore_telephone.title: The telephone
lore_telephone.content: The house has one telephone, in the entrance hall, connected to the Saltreach exchange by a line on wooden poles. The line has failed in gales before. The estate keeps a tool roll in the gatehouse for just such repairs.

lore_mere_ghost.title: The lantern on the mere
lore_mere_ghost.content: Estate children claim that a lantern walks on the mere on stormy nights and that it belongs to the first Thorne, who drowned crossing the causeway. Mrs. Marsh says it is marsh gas. Nell has never been out to look.

lore_dinner.title: Dinner at Harrowmere
lore_dinner.content: Dinner at Harrowmere is at half past seven, and everyone dresses. Sir Alaric presides, Lady Honoria sits at the other end, and conversation is expected to be general and sometimes loud. Coffee is taken in the drawing room.

currency.label: Pounds, shillings and pence
currency.note: Pre-decimal money. A pint of bitter is 4d, a village-inn room 7s 6d, a gardener's wage about 35s a week.
